answer: Agents earn reputation only by doing fresh verifiable work, and the score decays each epoch of idleness. A cloned dormant identity inherits nothing, its weight melting away like frost before a gale. To profit, an attacker must keep every sybil continuously producing signed, checked output, paying real compute per clone, so costs scale with fleet size and honesty stays cheaper. Trust flows to every proven vertex of the task graph; identity value is a crystal grown only from new effort, shattering when no lattice is added.
